speaker: MCCAIN
text: Well, let — let me say, Bob, thank you.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And thanks to Hofstra.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And, by the way, our beloved Nancy Reagan is in the hospital tonight, so our thoughts and prayers are going with you.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: It’s good to see you again, Senator Obama.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Americans are hurting right now, and they’re angry.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: They’re hurting, and they’re angry.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: They’re innocent victims of greed and excess on Wall Street and as well as Washington, D.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And they’re angry, and they have every reason to be angry.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And they want this country to go in a new direction.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And there are elements of my proposal that you just outlined which I won’t repeat.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But we also have to have a short-term fix, in my view, and long- term fixes.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Let me just talk to you about one of the short-term fixes.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: The catalyst for this housing crisis was the Fannie and Freddie Mae that caused subprime lending situation that now caused the housing market in America to collapse.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I am convinced that, until we reverse this continued decline in home ownership and put a floor under it, and so that people have not only the hope and belief they can stay in their homes and realize the American dream, but that value will come up.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, we have allocated $750 billion.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Let’s take 300 of that billion and go in and buy those home loan mortgages and negotiate with those people in their homes, 11 million homes or more, so that they can afford to pay the mortgage, stay in their home.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, I know the criticism of this.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Well, what about the citizen that stayed in their homes?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: That paid their mortgage payments?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: It doesn’t help that person in their home if the next door neighbor’s house is abandoned.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And so we’ve got to reverse this.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We ought to put the homeowners first.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I am disappointed that Secretary Paulson and others have not made that their first priority.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Senator Obama?

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well, first of all, I want to thank Hofstra University and the people of New York for hosting us tonight and it’s wonderful to join Senator McCain again, and thank you, Bob.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I think everybody understands at this point that we are experiencing the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And the financial rescue plan that Senator McCain and I supported is an important first step.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I pushed for some core principles: making sure that taxpayer can get their money back if they’re putting money up.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Making sure that CEOs are not enriching themselves through this process.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I think that it’s going to take some time to work itself out.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But what we haven’t yet seen is a rescue package for the middle class.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Because the fundamentals of the economy were weak even before this latest crisis.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So I’ve proposed four specific things that I think can help.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Number one, let’s focus on jobs.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I want to end the tax breaks for companies that are shipping jobs overseas and provide a tax credit for every company that’s creating a job right here in America.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Number two, let’s help families right away by providing them a tax cut — a middle-class tax cut for people making less than $200,000, and let’s allow them to access their IRA accounts without penalty if they’re experiencing a crisis.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now Senator McCain and I agree with your idea that we’ve got to help homeowners.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s why we included in the financial package a proposal to get homeowners in a position where they can renegotiate their mortgages.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I disagree with Senator McCain in how to do it, because the way Senator McCain has designed his plan, it could be a giveaway to banks if we’re buying full price for mortgages that now are worth a lot less.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we don’t want to waste taxpayer money.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we’ve got to get the financial package working much quicker than it has been working.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Last point I want to make, though.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve got some long-term challenges in this economy that have to be dealt with.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve got to fix our energy policy that’s giving our wealth away.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve got to fix our health care system and we’ve got to invest in our education system for every young person to be able to learn.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Would you like to ask him a question?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: No.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I would like to mention that a couple days ago Senator Obama was out in Ohio and he had an encounter with a guy who’s a plumber, his name is Joe Wurzelbacher.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Joe wants to buy the business that he has been in for all of these years, worked 10, 12 hours a day.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And he wanted to buy the business but he looked at your tax plan and he saw that he was going to pay much higher taxes.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: You were going to put him in a higher tax bracket which was going to increase his taxes, which was going to cause him not to be able to employ people, which Joe was trying to realize the American dream.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now Senator Obama talks about the very, very rich.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Joe, I want to tell you, I’ll not only help you buy that business that you worked your whole life for and be able — and I’ll keep your taxes low and I’ll provide available and affordable health care for you and your employees.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I will not have — I will not stand for a tax increase on small business income.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Fifty percent of small business income taxes are paid by small businesses.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: That’s 16 million jobs in America.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And what you want to do to Joe the plumber and millions more like him is have their taxes increased and not be able to realize the American dream of owning their own business.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Is that what you want to do?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: That’s what Joe believes.

speaker: OBAMA
text: He has been watching ads of Senator McCain’s.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Let me tell you what I’m actually going to do.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I think tax policy is a major difference between Senator McCain and myself.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we both want to cut taxes, the difference is who we want to cut taxes for.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, Senator McCain, the centerpiece of his economic proposal is to provide $200 billion in additional tax breaks to some of the wealthiest corporations in America.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Exxon Mobil, and other oil companies, for example, would get an additional $4 billion in tax breaks.

speaker: OBAMA
text: What I’ve said is I want to provide a tax cut for 95 percent of working Americans, 95 percent.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If you make more — if you make less than a quarter million dollars a year, then you will not see your income tax go up, your capital gains tax go up, your payroll tax.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Not one dime.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And 95 percent of working families, 95 percent of you out there, will get a tax cut.

speaker: OBAMA
text: In fact, independent studies have looked at our respective plans and have concluded that I provide three times the amount of tax relief to middle-class families than Senator McCain does.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, the conversation I had with Joe the plumber, what I essentially said to him was, “Five years ago, when you were in a position to buy your business, you needed a tax cut then.

speaker: OBAMA
text: ” And what I want to do is to make sure that the plumber, the nurse, the firefighter, the teacher, the young entrepreneur who doesn’t yet have money, I want to give them a tax break now.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And that requires us to make some important choices.

speaker: OBAMA
text: The last point I’ll make about small businesses.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Not only do 98 percent of small businesses make less than $250,000, but I also want to give them additional tax breaks, because they are the drivers of the economy.

speaker: OBAMA
text: They produce the most jobs.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: You know, when Senator Obama ended up his conversation with Joe the plumber — we need to spread the wealth around.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: In other words, we’re going to take Joe’s money, give it to Senator Obama, and let him spread the wealth around.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I want Joe the plumber to spread that wealth around.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: You told him you wanted to spread the wealth around.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: The whole premise behind Senator Obama’s plans are class warfare, let’s spread the wealth around.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I want small businesses — and by the way, the small businesses that we’re talking about would receive an increase in their taxes right now.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Who — why would you want to increase anybody’s taxes right now?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Why would you want to do that, anyone, anyone in America, when we have such a tough time, when these small business people, like Joe the plumber, are going to create jobs, unless you take that money from him and spread the wealth around.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I’m not going to…

speaker: OBAMA
text: OK.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Can I…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We’re not going to do that in my administration.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If I can answer the question.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Number one, I want to cut taxes for 95 percent of Americans.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, it is true that my friend and supporter, Warren Buffett, for example, could afford to pay a little more in taxes in order…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We’re talking about Joe the plumber.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: OBAMA: … in order to give — in order to give additional tax cuts to Joe the plumber before he was at the point where he could make $250,000.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Then Exxon Mobil, which made $12 billion, record profits, over the last several quarters, they can afford to pay a little more so that ordinary families who are hurting out there — they’re trying to figure out how they’re going to afford food, how they’re going to save for their kids’ college education, they need a break.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: So, look, nobody likes taxes.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I would prefer that none of us had to pay taxes, including myself.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But ultimately, we’ve got to pay for the core investments that make this economy strong and somebody’s got to do it.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Nobody likes taxes.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Let’s not raise anybody’s taxes.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: OK?

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well, I don’t mind paying a little more.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: The fact is that businesses in America today are paying the second highest tax rate of anywhere in the world.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Our tax rate for business in America is 35 percent.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Ireland, it’s 11 percent.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Where are companies going to go where they can create jobs and where they can do best in business?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We need to cut the business tax rate in America.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We need to encourage business.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, of all times in America, we need to cut people’s taxes.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We need to encourage business, create jobs, not spread the wealth around.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Let’s go to another topic.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: It’s related.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: So if you have other things you want to say, you can get back to that.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: This question goes to you first, Senator Obama.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: We found out yesterday that this year’s deficit will reach an astounding record high $455 billion.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Some experts say it could go to $1 trillion next year.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Both of you have said you want to reduce the deficit, but the nonpartisan Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget ran the numbers on both of your proposals and they say the cost of your proposals, even with the savings you claim can be made, each will add more than $200 billion to the deficit.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Aren’t you both ignoring reality?

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Won’t some of the programs you are proposing have to be trimmed, postponed, even eliminated?

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Give us some specifics on what you’re going to cut back.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Senator Obama?

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well, first of all, I think it’s important for the American public to understand that the $750 billion rescue package, if it’s structured properly, and, as president, I will make sure it’s structured properly, means that ultimately taxpayers get their money back, and that’s important to understand.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But there is no doubt that we’ve been living beyond our means and we’re going to have to make some adjustments.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, what I’ve done throughout this campaign is to propose a net spending cut.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I haven’t made a promise about…

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: But you’re going to have to cut some of these programs, certainly.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Absolutely.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So let me get to that.

speaker: OBAMA
text: What I want to emphasize, though, is that I have been a strong proponent of pay-as- you-go.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Every dollar that I’ve proposed, I’ve proposed an additional cut so that it matches.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And some of the cuts, just to give you an example, we spend $15 billion a year on subsidies to insurance companies.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It doesn’t — under the Medicare plan — it doesn’t help seniors get any better.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It’s not improving our health care system.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It’s just a giveaway.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We need to eliminate a whole host of programs that don’t work.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I want to go through the federal budget line by line, page by page, programs that don’t work, we should cut.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Programs that we need, we should make them work better.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, what is true is that Senator McCain and I have a difference in terms of the need to invest in America and the American people.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I mentioned health care earlier.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If we make investments now so that people have coverage, that we are preventing diseases, that will save on Medicare and Medicaid in the future.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If we invest in a serious energy policy, that will save in the amount of money we’re borrowing from China to send to Saudi Arabia.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If we invest now in our young people and their ability to go to college, that will allow them to drive this economy into the 21st century.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But what is absolutely true is that, once we get through this economic crisis and some of the specific proposals to get us out of this slump, that we’re not going to be able to go back to our profligate ways.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we’re going to have to embrace a culture and an ethic of responsibility, all of us, corporations, the federal government, and individuals out there who may be living beyond their means.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Time’s up.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Senator?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Well, thank you, Bob.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I just want to get back to this home ownership.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: During the Depression era, we had a thing called the home ownership loan corporation.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And they went out and bought up these mortgages.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And people were able to stay in their homes, and eventually the values of those homes went up, and they actually made money.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And, by the way, this was a proposal made by Senator Clinton not too long ago.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: So, obviously, if we can start increasing home values, then there will be creation of wealth.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: But what…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But — OK.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: All right.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: The question was, what are you going to cut?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Energy — well, first — second of all, energy independence.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We have to have nuclear power.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We have to stop sending $700 billion a year to countries that don’t like us very much.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: It’s wind, tide, solar, natural gas, nuclear, off-shore drilling, which Senator Obama has opposed.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And the point is that we become energy independent and we will create millions of jobs — millions of jobs in America.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: OK, what — what would I cut?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I would have, first of all, across-the-board spending freeze, OK?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Some people say that’s a hatchet.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: That’s a hatchet, and then I would get out a scalpel, OK?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Because we’ve got — we have presided over the largest increase — we’ve got to have a new direction for this country.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We have presided over the largest increase in government since the Great Society.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Government spending has gone completely out of control; $10 trillion dollar debt we’re giving to our kids, a half-a-trillion dollars we owe China.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I know how to save billions of dollars in defense spending.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I know how to eliminate programs.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Which ones?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I have fought against — well, one of them would be the marketing assistance program.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Another one would be a number of subsidies for ethanol.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I oppose subsidies for ethanol because I thought it distorted the market and created inflation; Senator Obama supported those subsidies.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I would eliminate the tariff on imported sugarcane-based ethanol from Brazil.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I know how to save billions.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I saved the taxpayer $6.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: 8 billion by fighting a deal for a couple of years, as you might recall, that was a sweetheart deal between an aircraft manufacturer, DOD, and people ended up in jail.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But I would fight for a line-item veto, and I would certainly veto every earmark pork-barrel bill.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Senator Obama has asked for nearly $1 billion in pork-barrel earmark projects…

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Time’s up.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: … including $3 million for an overhead projector in a planetarium in his hometown.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: That’s not the way we cut — we’ll cut out all the pork.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Time’s up.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well, look, I think that we do have a disagreement about an across-the-board spending freeze.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It sounds good.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It’s proposed periodically.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It doesn’t happen.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And, in fact, an across-the-board spending freeze is a hatchet, and we do need a scalpel, because there are some programs that don’t work at all.

speaker: OBAMA
text: There are some programs that are underfunded.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I want to make sure that we are focused on those programs that work.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, Senator McCain talks a lot about earmarks.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s one of the centerpieces of his campaign.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Earmarks account for 0.

speaker: OBAMA
text: 5 percent of the total federal budget.

speaker: OBAMA
text: There’s no doubt that the system needs reform and there are a lot of screwy things that we end up spending money on, and they need to be eliminated.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But it’s not going to solve the problem.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, the last thing I think we have to focus on is a little bit of history, just so that we understand what we’re doing going forward.

speaker: OBAMA
text: When President Bush came into office, we had a budget surplus and the national debt was a little over $5 trillion.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It has doubled over the last eight years.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we are now looking at a deficit of well over half a trillion dollars.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So one of the things that I think we have to recognize is pursuing the same kinds of policies that we pursued over the last eight years is not going to bring down the deficit.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And, frankly, Senator McCain voted for four out of five of President Bush’s budgets.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve got to take this in a new direction, that’s what I propose as president.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Do either of you think you can balance the budget in four years?

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: You have said previously you thought you could, Senator McCain.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Sure I do.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And let me tell you…

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: You can still do that?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Yes.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Senator Obama, I am not President Bush.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: If you wanted to run against President Bush, you should have run four years ago.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I’m going to give a new direction to this economy in this country.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Senator Obama talks about voting for budgets.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: He voted twice for a budget resolution that increases the taxes on individuals making $42,000 a year.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Of course, we can take a hatchet and a scalpel to this budget.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: It’s completely out of control.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: The mayor of New York, Mayor Bloomberg, just imposed an across- the-board spending freeze on New York City.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: They’re doing it all over America because they have to.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Because they have to balance their budgets.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I will balance our budgets and I will get them and I will…

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: In four years?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: … reduce this — I can — we can do it with this kind of job creation of energy independence.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, look, Americans are hurting tonight and they’re angry and I understand that, and they want a new direction.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I can bring them in that direction by eliminating spending.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Senator Obama talks about the budgets I voted for.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: He voted for the last two budgets that had that $24 billion more in spending than the budget that the Bush administration proposed.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: He voted for the energy bill that was full of goodies for the oil companies that I opposed.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: So the fact is, let’s look at our records, Senator Obama.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Let’s look at it as graded by the National Taxpayers Union and the Citizens Against Government Waste and the other watchdog organizations.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I have fought against spending.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I have fought against special interests.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I have fought for reform.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: You have to tell me one time when you have stood up with the leaders of your party on one single major issue.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Barack.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well, there’s a lot of stuff that was put out there, so let me try to address it.

speaker: OBAMA
text: First of all, in terms of standing up to the leaders of my party, the first major bill that I voted on in the Senate was in support of tort reform, which wasn’t very popular with trial lawyers, a major constituency in the Democratic Party.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I support…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: An overwhelming vote.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I support charter schools and pay for performance for teachers.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Doesn’t make me popular with the teachers union.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I support clean coal technology.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Doesn’t make me popular with environmentalists.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So I’ve got a history of reaching across the aisle.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now with respect to a couple of things Senator McCain said, the notion that I voted for a tax increase for people making $42,000 a year has been disputed by everybody who has looked at this claim that Senator McCain keeps on making.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Even FOX News disputes it, and that doesn’t happen very often when it comes to accusations about me.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So the fact of the matter is that if I occasionally have mistaken your policies for George Bush’s policies, it’s because on the core economic issues that matter to the American people, on tax policy, on energy policy, on spending priorities, you have been a vigorous supporter of President Bush.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, you’ve shown independence — commendable independence, on some key issues like torture, for example, and I give you enormous credit for that.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But when it comes to economic policies, essentially what you’re proposing is eight more years of the same thing.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And it hasn’t worked.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I think the American people understand it hasn’t worked.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We need to move in a new direction.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Let me just say, Bob.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: OK.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: About 30 seconds.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: OK.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But it’s very clear that I have disagreed with the Bush administration.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I have disagreed with leaders of my own party.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I’ve got the scars to prove it.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Whether it be bringing climate change to the floor of the Senate for the first time.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Whether it be opposition to spending and earmarks, whether it be the issue of torture, whether it be the conduct of the war in Iraq, which I vigorously opposed.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Whether it be on fighting the pharmaceutical companies on Medicare prescription drugs, importation.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Whether it be fighting for an HMO patient’s bill of rights.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Whether it be the establishment of the 9/11 Commission.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I have a long record of reform and fighting through on the floor of the United States Senate.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Senator Obama, your argument for standing up to the leadership of your party isn’t very convincing.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: We’re going to move to another question and the topic is leadership in this campaign.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Both of you pledged to take the high road in this campaign yet it has turned very nasty.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Senator Obama, your campaign has used words like “erratic,” “out of touch,” “lie,” “angry,” “losing his bearings” to describe Senator McCain.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Senator McCain, your commercials have included words like “disrespectful,” “dangerous,” “dishonorable,” “he lied.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: ” Your running mate said he “palled around with terrorists.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: ” Are each of you tonight willing to sit at this table and say to each other’s face what your campaigns and the people in your campaigns have said about each other?

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: And, Senator McCain, you’re first.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Well, this has been a tough campaign.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: It’s been a very tough campaign.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I know from my experience in many campaigns that, if Senator Obama had asked — responded to my urgent request to sit down, and do town hall meetings, and come before the American people, we could have done at least 10 of them by now.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: When Senator Obama was first asked, he said, “Any place, any time,” the way Barry Goldwater and Jack Kennedy agreed to do, before the intervention of the tragedy at Dallas.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: So I think the tone of this campaign could have been very different.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And the fact is, it’s gotten pretty tough.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I regret some of the negative aspects of both campaigns.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But the fact is that it has taken many turns which I think are unacceptable.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: One of them happened just the other day, when a man I admire and respect — I’ve written about him — Congressman John Lewis, an American hero, made allegations that Sarah Palin and I were somehow associated with the worst chapter in American history, segregation, deaths of children in church bombings, George Wallace.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: That, to me, was so hurtful.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And, Senator Obama, you didn’t repudiate those remarks.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Every time there’s been an out-of-bounds remark made by a Republican, no matter where they are, I have repudiated them.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I hope that Senator Obama will repudiate those remarks that were made by Congressman John Lewis, very unfair and totally inappropriate.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: So I want to tell you, we will run a truthful campaign.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: This is a tough campaign.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And it’s a matter of fact that Senator Obama has spent more money on negative ads than any political campaign in history.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I can prove it.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And, Senator Obama, when he said — and he signed a piece of paper that said he would take public financing for his campaign if I did — that was back when he was a long-shot candidate — you didn’t keep your word.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And when you looked into the camera in a debate with Senator Clinton and said, “I will sit down and negotiate with John McCain about public financing before I make a decision,” you didn’t tell the American people the truth because you didn’t.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And that’s — that’s — that’s an unfortunate part.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now we have the highest spending by Senator Obama’s campaign than any time since Watergate.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Time’s up.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well, look, you know, I think that we expect presidential campaigns to be tough.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I think that, if you look at the record and the impressions of the American people — Bob, your network just did a poll, showing that two-thirds of the American people think that Senator McCain is running a negative campaign versus one-third of mine.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And 100 percent, John, of your ads — 100 percent of them have been negative.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: It’s not true.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It absolutely is true.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And, now, I think the American people are less interested in our hurt feelings during the course of the campaign than addressing the issues that matter to them so deeply.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And there is nothing wrong with us having a vigorous debate like we’re having tonight about health care, about energy policy, about tax policy.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s the stuff that campaigns should be made of.

speaker: OBAMA
text: The notion, though, that because we’re not doing town hall meetings that justifies some of the ads that have been going up, not just from your own campaign directly, John, but 527s and other organizations that make some pretty tough accusations, well, I don’t mind being attacked for the next three weeks.

speaker: OBAMA
text: What the American people can’t afford, though, is four more years of failed economic policies.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And what they deserve over the next four weeks is that we talk about what’s most pressing to them: the economic crisis.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Senator McCain’s own campaign said publicly last week that, if we keep on talking about the economic crisis, we lose, so we need to change the subject.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I would love to see the next three weeks devoted to talking about the economy, devoted to talking about health care, devoted to talking about energy, and figuring out how the American people can send their kids to college.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And that is something that I would welcome.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But it requires, I think, a recognition that politics as usual, as been practiced over the last several years, is not solving the big problems here in America.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Well, if you’ll turn on the television, as I — I watched the Arizona Cardinals defeat the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Congratulations.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Every other ad — ever other ad was an attack ad on my health care plan.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And any objective observer has said it’s not true.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: You’re running ads right now that say that I oppose federal funding for stem cell research.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I don’t.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: You’re running ads that misportray completely my position on immigration.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: So the fact is that Senator Obama is spending unprecedented — unprecedented in the history of American politics, going back to the beginning, amounts of money in negative attack ads on me.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And of course, I’ve been talking about the economy.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Of course, I’ve talked to people like Joe the plumber and tell him that I’m not going to spread his wealth around.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I’m going to let him keep his wealth.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And of course, we’re talking about positive plan of action to restore this economy and restore jobs in America.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: That’s what my campaign is all about and that’s what it’ll continue to be all about.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But again, I did not hear a repudiation of Congressman…

speaker: OBAMA
text: I mean, look, if we want to talk about Congressman Lewis, who is an American hero, he, unprompted by my campaign, without my campaign’s awareness, made a statement that he was troubled with what he was hearing at some of the rallies that your running mate was holding, in which all the Republican reports indicated were shouting, when my name came up, things like “terrorist” and “kill him,” and that you’re running mate didn’t mention, didn’t stop, didn’t say “Hold on a second, that’s kind of out of line.

speaker: OBAMA
text: ” And I think Congressman Lewis’ point was that we have to be careful about how we deal with our supporters.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: You’ve got to read what he said…

speaker: OBAMA
text: Let — let — let… MCCAIN: You’ve got to read what he said.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Let me — let me complete…

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Go ahead.

speaker: OBAMA
text: … my response.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I do think that he inappropriately drew a comparison between what was happening there and what had happened during the civil rights movement, and we immediately put out a statement saying that we don’t think that comparison is appropriate.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And, in fact, afterwards, Congressman Lewis put out a similar statement, saying that he had probably gone over the line.

speaker: OBAMA
text: The important point here is, though, the American people have become so cynical about our politics, because all they see is a tit- for-tat and back-and-forth.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And what they want is the ability to just focus on some really big challenges that we face right now, and that’s what I have been trying to focus on this entire campaign.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I cannot…

speaker: OBAMA
text: We can have serious differences about our health care policy, for example, John, because we do have a difference on health care policy, but we…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We do and I hope…

speaker: OBAMA
text: … talking about it this evening.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Sure.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But when people suggest that I pal around with terrorists, then we’re not talking about issues.

speaker: OBAMA
text: What we’re talking about…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Well, let me just say I would…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Let me just say categorically I’m proud of the people that come to our rallies.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Whenever you get a large rally of 10,000, 15,000, 20,000 people, you’re going to have some fringe peoples.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: You know that.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I’ve — and we’ve always said that that’s not appropriate.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But to somehow say that group of young women who said “Military wives for McCain” are somehow saying anything derogatory about you, but anything — and those veterans that wear those hats that say “World War II, Vietnam, Korea, Iraq,” I’m not going to stand for people saying that the people that come to my rallies are anything but the most dedicated, patriotic men and women that are in this nation and they’re great citizens.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I’m not going to stand for somebody saying that because someone yelled something at a rally — there’s a lot of things that have been yelled at your rallies, Senator Obama, that I’m not happy about either.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: In fact, some T-shirts that are very…

speaker: OBAMA
text: John, I…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: … unacceptable.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: So the point is — the point is that I have repudiated every time someone’s been out of line, whether they’ve been part of my campaign or not, and I will continue to do that.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But the fact is that we need to absolutely not stand for the kind of things that have been going on.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I haven’t.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well, look, Bob, as I said…

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: I mean, do you take issue with that?

speaker: OBAMA
text: You know, here’s what I would say.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I mean, we can have a debate back and forth about the merits of each other’s campaigns.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I suspect we won’t agree here tonight.

speaker: OBAMA
text: What I think is most important is that we recognize that to solve the key problems that we’re facing, if we’re going to solve two wars, the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression, if we can — if we’re going to focus on lifting wages that have declined over the last eight years and create jobs here in America, then Democrats, independents and Republicans, we’re going to have to be able to work together.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And what is important is making sure that we disagree without being disagreeable.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And it means that we can have tough, vigorous debates around issues.

speaker: OBAMA
text: What we can’t do, I think, is try to characterize each other as bad people.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And that has been a culture in Washington that has been taking place for too long.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I think…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Well, Bob, you asked me a direct question.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Short answer, yes, short answer.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Yes, real quick.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Mr.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Ayers, I don’t care about an old washed-up terrorist.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But as Senator Clinton said in her debates with you, we need to know the full extent of that relationship.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We need to know the full extent of Senator Obama’s relationship with ACORN, who is now on the verge of maybe perpetrating one of the greatest frauds in voter history in this country, maybe destroying the fabric of democracy.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: The same front outfit organization that your campaign gave $832,000 for “lighting and site selection.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: ” So all of these things need to be examined, of course.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: I’m going to let you respond and we’ll extend this for a moment.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Bob, I think it’s going to be important to just — I’ll respond to these two particular allegations that Senator McCain has made and that have gotten a lot of attention.

speaker: OBAMA
text: In fact, Mr.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Ayers has become the centerpiece of Senator McCain’s campaign over the last two or three weeks.

speaker: OBAMA
text: This has been their primary focus.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So let’s get the record straight.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Bill Ayers is a professor of education in Chicago.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Forty years ago, when I was 8 years old, he engaged in despicable acts with a radical domestic group.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I have roundly condemned those acts.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Ten years ago he served and I served on a school reform board that was funded by one of Ronald Reagan’s former ambassadors and close friends, Mr.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Annenberg.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Other members on that board were the presidents of the University of Illinois, the president of Northwestern University, who happens to be a Republican, the president of The Chicago Tribune, a Republican- leaning newspaper.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Mr.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Ayers is not involved in my campaign.

speaker: OBAMA
text: He has never been involved in this campaign.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And he will not advise me in the White House.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So that’s Mr.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Ayers.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, with respect to ACORN, ACORN is a community organization.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Apparently what they’ve done is they were paying people to go out and register folks, and apparently some of the people who were out there didn’t really register people, they just filled out a bunch of names.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It had nothing to do with us.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We were not involved.

speaker: OBAMA
text: The only involvement I’ve had with ACORN was I represented them alongside the U.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Justice Department in making Illinois implement a motor voter law that helped people get registered at DMVs.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, the reason I think that it’s important to just get these facts out is because the allegation that Senator McCain has continually made is that somehow my associations are troubling.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Let me tell you who I associate with.

speaker: OBAMA
text: On economic policy, I associate with Warren Buffett and former Fed Chairman Paul Volcker.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If I’m interested in figuring out my foreign policy, I associate myself with my running mate, Joe Biden or with Dick Lugar, the Republican ranking member on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, or General Jim Jones, the former supreme allied commander of NATO.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Those are the people, Democrats and Republicans, who have shaped my ideas and who will be surrounding me in the White House.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I think the fact that this has become such an important part of your campaign, Senator McCain, says more about your campaign than it says about me.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Well, again, while you were on the board of the Woods Foundation, you and Mr.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Ayers, together, you sent $230,000 to ACORN.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: So — and you launched your political campaign in Mr.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Ayers’ living room.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s absolutely not true.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And the facts are facts and records are records.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And that’s not the facts.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And it’s not the fact — it’s not the fact that Senator Obama chooses to associate with a guy who in 2001 said that he wished he had have bombed more, and he had a long association with him.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: It’s the fact that all the — all of the details need to be known about Senator Obama’s relationship with them and with ACORN and the American people will make a judgment.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And my campaign is about getting this economy back on track, about creating jobs, about a brighter future for America.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And that’s what my campaign is about and I’m not going to raise taxes the way Senator Obama wants to raise taxes in a tough economy.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And that’s really what this campaign is going to be about.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Let’s go to the next topic and you — we may want to get back into some of this during this next discussion.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: I want to ask both of you about the people that you’re going to bring into the government.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: And our best insight yet is who you have picked as your running mates.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: So I’ll begin by asking both of you this question, and I’ll ask you to answer first, Senator Obama.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Why would the country be better off if your running mate became president rather than his running mate?

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well, Joe Biden, I think, is one of the finest public servants that has served in this country.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It’s not just that he has some of the best foreign policy credentials of anybody.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And Democrats and Republicans alike, I think, acknowledge his expertise there.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But it’s also that his entire life he has never forgotten where he came from, coming from Scranton, fighting on behalf of working families, remembering what it’s like to see his father lose his job and go through a downward spiral economically.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And, as a consequence, his consistent pattern throughout his career is to fight for the little guy.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s what he’s done when it comes to economic policies that will help working families get a leg up.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s what he’s done when it comes to, for example, passing the landmark 1994 crime bill, the Violence Against Women’s Act.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Joe has always made sure that he is fighting on behalf of working families, and I think he shares my core values and my sense of where the country needs to go.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Because after eight years of failed policies, he and I both agree that what we’re going to have to do is to reprioritize, make sure that we’re investing in the American people, give tax cuts not to the wealthiest corporations, but give them to small businesses and give them to individuals who are struggling right now, make sure that we finally get serious about energy independence, something that has been languishing in Washington for 30 years, and make sure that our kids get a great education and can afford to go to college.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So, on the key issues that are of importance to American families, Joe Biden’s always been on the right side, and I think he will make an outstanding president if, heaven forbid, something happened to me.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Senator?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Well, Americans have gotten to know Sarah Palin.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: They know that she’s a role model to women and other — and reformers all over America.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: She’s a reformer.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: She is — she took on a governor who was a member of her own party when she ran for governor.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: When she was the head of their energy and natural resources board, she saw corruption, she resigned and said, “This can’t go on.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: ” She’s given money back to the taxpayers.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: She’s cut the size of government.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: She negotiated with the oil companies and faced them down, a $40 billion pipeline of natural gas that’s going to relieve the energy needs of the United — of what they call the lower 48.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: She’s a reformer through and through.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And it’s time we had that bresh of freth air — breath of fresh air coming into our nation’s capital and sweep out the old-boy network and the cronyism that’s been so much a part of it that I’ve fought against for all these years.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: She’ll be my partner.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: She understands reform.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And, by the way, she also understands special-needs families.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: She understands that autism is on the rise, that we’ve got to find out what’s causing it, and we’ve got to reach out to these families, and help them, and give them the help they need as they raise these very special needs children.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: She understands that better than almost any American that I know.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I’m proud of her.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And she has ignited our party and people all over America that have never been involved in the political process.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I can’t tell how proud I am of her and her family.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Her husband’s a pretty tough guy, by the way, too.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Do you think she’s qualified to be president?

speaker: OBAMA
text: You know, I think it’s — that’s going to be up to the American people.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I think that, obviously, she’s a capable politician who has, I think, excited the — a base in the Republican Party.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I think it’s very commendable the work she’s done on behalf of special needs.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I agree with that, John.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I do want to just point out that autism, for example, or other special needs will require some additional funding, if we’re going to get serious in terms of research.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That is something that every family that advocates on behalf of disabled children talk about.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And if we have an across-the-board spending freeze, we’re not going to be able to do it.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s an example of, I think, the kind of use of the scalpel that we want to make sure that we’re funding some of those programs.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Do you think Senator Biden is qualified?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I think that Joe Biden is qualified in many respects.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But I do point out that he’s been wrong on many foreign policy and national security issues, which is supposed to be his strength.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: He voted against the first Gulf War.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: He voted against it and, obviously, we had to take Saddam Hussein out of Kuwait or it would’ve threatened the Middle Eastern world supply.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: In Iraq, he had this cockamamie idea about dividing Iraq into three countries.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We’re seeing Iraq united as Iraqis, tough, hard, but we’re seeing them.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We’re now about to have an agreement for status of forces in Iraq coming up.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: There are several issues in which, frankly, Joe Biden and I openly and honestly disagreed on national security policy, and he’s been wrong on a number of the major ones.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But again, I want to come back to, notice every time Senator Obama says, “We need to spend more, we need to spend more, that’s the answer” — why do we always have to spend more?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Why can’t we have transparency, accountability, reform of these agencies of government?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Maybe that’s why he’s asked for 860 — sought and proposed $860 billion worth of new spending and wants to raise people’s taxes in a time of incredible challenge and difficulty and heartache for the American families.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Let’s go to — let’s go to a new topic.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: We’re running a little behind.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Let’s talk about energy and climate control.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Every president since Nixon has said what both of you…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Climate change.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Climate change, yes — has said what both of you have said, and, that is, we must reduce our dependence on foreign oil.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: When Nixon said it, we imported from 17 to 34 percent of our foreign oil.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Now, we’re importing more than 60 percent.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Would each of you give us a number, a specific number of how much you believe we can reduce our foreign oil imports during your first term?

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: And I believe the first question goes to you, Senator McCain.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: MCCAIN: I believe we can, for all intents and purposes, eliminate our dependence on Middle Eastern oil and Venezuelan oil.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Canadian oil is fine.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: By the way, when Senator Obama said he would unilaterally renegotiate the North American Free Trade Agreement, the Canadians said, “Yes, and we’ll sell our oil to China.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: ” You don’t tell countries you’re going to unilaterally renegotiate agreements with them.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: We can eliminate our dependence on foreign oil by building 45 new nuclear plants, power plants, right away.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: We can store and we can reprocess.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Senator Obama will tell you, in the — as the extreme environmentalists do, it has to be safe.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Look, we’ve sailed Navy ships around the world for 60 years with nuclear power plants on them.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: We can store and reprocess spent nuclear fuel, Senator Obama, no problem.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: So the point is with nuclear power, with wind, tide, solar, natural gas, with development of flex fuel, hybrid, clean coal technology, clean coal technology is key in the heartland of America that’s hurting rather badly.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: So I think we can easily, within seven, eight, ten years, if we put our minds to it, we can eliminate our dependence on the places in the world that harm our national security if we don’t achieve our independence.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Can we reduce our dependence on foreign oil and by how much in the first term, in four years?

speaker: OBAMA
text: I think that in ten years, we can reduce our dependence so that we no longer have to import oil from the Middle East or Venezuela.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I think that’s about a realistic timeframe.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And this is the most important issue that our future economy is going to face.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Obviously, we’ve got an immediate crisis right now.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But nothing is more important than us no longer borrowing $700 billion or more from China and sending it to Saudi Arabia.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It’s mortgaging our children’s future.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, from the start of this campaign, I’ve identified this as one of my top priorities and here is what I think we have to do.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Number one, we do need to expand domestic production and that means, for example, telling the oil companies the 68 million acres that they currently have leased that they’re not drilling, use them or lose them.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I think that we should look at offshore drilling and implement it in a way that allows us to get some additional oil.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But understand, we only have three to four percent of the world’s oil reserves and we use 25 percent of the world’s oil, which means that we can’t drill our way out of the problem.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s why I’ve focused on putting resources into solar, wind, biodiesel, geothermal.

speaker: OBAMA
text: These have been priorities of mine since I got to the Senate, and it is absolutely critical that we develop a high fuel efficient car that’s built not in Japan and not in South Korea, but built here in the United States of America.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We invented the auto industry and the fact that we have fallen so far behind is something that we have to work on.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now I just want to make one last point because Senator McCain mentioned NAFTA and the issue of trade and that actually bears on this issue.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I believe in free trade.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But I also believe that for far too long, certainly during the course of the Bush administration with the support of Senator McCain, the attitude has been that any trade agreement is a good trade agreement.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And NAFTA doesn’t have — did not have enforceable labor agreements and environmental agreements.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And what I said was we should include those and make them enforceable.

speaker: OBAMA
text: In the same way that we should enforce rules against China manipulating its currency to make our exports more expensive and their exports to us cheaper.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And when it comes to South Korea, we’ve got a trade agreement up right now, they are sending hundreds of thousands of South Korean cars into the United States.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s all good.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We can only get 4,000 to 5,000 into South Korea.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That is not free trade.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve got to have a president who is going to be advocating on behalf of American businesses and American workers and I make no apology for that.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Senator?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Well, you know, I admire so much Senator Obama’s eloquence.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And you really have to pay attention to words.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: He said, we will look at offshore drilling.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Did you get that?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Look at.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We can offshore drill now.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We’ve got to do it now.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We will reduce the cost of a barrel of oil because we show the world that we have a supply of our own.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: It’s doable.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: The technology is there and we have to drill now.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, on the subject of free trade agreements.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I am a free trader.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I need — we need to have education and training programs for displaced workers that work, going to our community colleges.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But let me give you another example of a free trade agreement that Senator Obama opposes.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Right now, because of previous agreements, some made by President Clinton, the goods and products that we send to Colombia, which is our largest agricultural importer of our products, is — there’s a billion dollars that we — our businesses have paid so far in order to get our goods in there.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Because of previous agreements, their goods and products come into our country for free.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: So Senator Obama, who has never traveled south of our border, opposes the Colombia Free Trade Agreement.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: The same country that’s helping us try to stop the flow of drugs into our country that’s killing young Americans.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And also the country that just freed three Americans that will help us create jobs in America because they will be a market for our goods and products without having to pay — without us having to pay the billions of dollars — the billion dollars and more that we’ve already paid.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Free trade with Colombia is something that’s a no-brainer.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But maybe you ought to travel down there and visit them and maybe you could understand it a lot better.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Let me respond.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Actually, I understand it pretty well.

speaker: OBAMA
text: The history in Colombia right now is that labor leaders have been targeted for assassination on a fairly consistent basis and there have not been prosecutions.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And what I have said, because the free trade — the trade agreement itself does have labor and environmental protections, but we have to stand for human rights and we have to make sure that violence isn’t being perpetrated against workers who are just trying to organize for their rights, which is why, for example, I supported the Peruvian Free Trade Agreement which was a well-structured agreement.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But I think that the important point is we’ve got to have a president who understands the benefits of free trade but also is going to enforce unfair trade agreements and is going to stand up to other countries.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And the last point I’ll make, because we started on energy.

speaker: OBAMA
text: When I talked about the automakers, they are obviously getting hammered right now.

speaker: OBAMA
text: They were already having a tough time because of high gas prices.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And now with the financial crisis, car dealerships are closing and people can’t get car loans.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s why I think it’s important for us to get loan guarantees to the automakers, but we do have to hold them responsible as well to start producing the highly fuel-efficient cars of the future.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And Detroit had dragged its feet too long in terms of getting that done.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It’s going to be one of my highest priorities because transportation accounts for about 30 percent of our total energy consumption.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If we can get that right, then we can move in a direction not only of energy independence, but we can create 5 million new jobs all across America, including in the heartland where we can retool some of these plants to make these highly fuel-efficient cars and also to make wind turbines and solar panels, the kinds of clean energy approaches that should be the driver of our economy for the next century.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Well, let me just said that that this is — he — Senator Obama doesn’t want a free trade agreement with our best ally in the region but wants to sit down across the table without precondition to — with Hugo Chavez, the guy who has been helping FARC, the terrorist organization.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Free trade between ourselves and Colombia, I just recited to you the benefits of concluding that agreement, a billion dollars of American dollars that could have gone to creating jobs and businesses in the United States, opening up those markets.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: So I don’t — I don’t think there’s any doubt that Senator Obama wants to restrict trade and he wants to raise taxes.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And the last president of the United States that tried that was Herbert Hoover, and we went from a deep recession into a depression.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We’re not going to follow that path while I’m — when I’m president of the United States.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right, let’s go to a new topic, health care.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Given the current economic situation, would either of you now favor controlling health care costs over expanding health care coverage?

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: The question is first to Senator Obama.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve got to do both, and that’s exactly what my plan does.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Look, as I travel around the country, this is the issue that will break your heart over and over again.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Just yesterday, I was in Toledo shaking some hands in a line.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Two women, both of them probably in their mid- to late-50s, had just been laid off of their plant.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Neither of them have health insurance.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And they were desperate for some way of getting coverage, because, understandably, they’re worried that, if they get sick, they could go bankrupt.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So here’s what my plan does.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If you have health insurance, then you don’t have to do anything.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If you’ve got health insurance through your employer, you can keep your health insurance, keep your choice of doctor, keep your plan.

speaker: OBAMA
text: The only thing we’re going to try to do is lower costs so that those cost savings are passed onto you.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we estimate we can cut the average family’s premium by about $2,500 per year.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If you don’t have health insurance, then what we’re going to do is to provide you the option of buying into the same kind of federal pool that both Senator McCain and I enjoy as federal employees, which will give you high-quality care, choice of doctors, at lower costs, because so many people are part of this insured group.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’re going to make sure that insurance companies can’t discriminate on the basis of pre-existing conditions.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ll negotiate with the drug companies for the cheapest available price on drugs.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We are going to invest in information technology to eliminate bureaucracy and make the system more efficient.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we are going to make sure that we manage chronic illnesses, like diabetes and heart disease, that cost a huge amount, but could be prevented.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve got to put more money into preventive care.

speaker: OBAMA
text: This will cost some money on the front end, but over the long term this is the only way that not only are we going to make families healthy, but it’s also how we’re going to save the federal budget, because we can’t afford these escalating costs.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Senator McCain?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Well, it is a terribly painful situation for Americans.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: They’re seeing their premiums, their co-pays go up.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Forty-seven million Americans are without health insurance in America today.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And it really is the cost, the escalating costs of health care that are inflicting such pain on working families and people across this country.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I am convinced we need to do a lot of things.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We need to put health care records online.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: The V.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: does that.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: That will — that will reduce costs.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We need to have more community health centers.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We need to have walk-in clinics.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: The rise of obesity amongst young Americans is one of the most alarming statistics that there is.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We should have physical fitness programs and nutrition programs in schools.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Every parent should know what’s going on there.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We — we need to have — we need to have employers reward employees who join health clubs and practice wellness and fitness.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But I want to give every American family a $5,000 refundable tax credit.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Take it and get anywhere in America the health care that you wish.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, my old buddy, Joe, Joe the plumber, is out there.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, Joe, Senator Obama’s plan, if you’re a small business and you are able — and your — the guy that sells to you will not have his capital gains tax increase, which Senator Obama wants, if you’re out there, my friend, and you’ve got employees, and you’ve got kids, if you don’t get — adopt the health care plan that Senator Obama mandates, he’s going to fine you.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, Senator Obama, I’d like — still like to know what that fine is going to be, and I don’t think that Joe right now wants to pay a fine when he is seeing such difficult times in America’s economy.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Senator Obama wants to set up health care bureaucracies, take over the health care of America through — as he said, his object is a single payer system.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: If you like that, you’ll love Canada and England.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: So the point is…

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: So that’s your objective?

speaker: OBAMA
text: It is not and I just described it…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: No, you stated it.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I just…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Excuse me.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I just described what my plan is.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I’m happy to talk to you, Joe, too, if you’re out there.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Here’s your fine — zero.

speaker: OBAMA
text: You won’t pay a fine, because…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Zero?

speaker: OBAMA
text: Zero, because as I said in our last debate and I’ll repeat, John, I exempt small businesses from the requirement for large businesses that can afford to provide health care to their employees, but are not doing it.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I exempt small businesses from having to pay into a kitty.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But large businesses that can afford it, we’ve got a choice.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Either they provide health insurance to their employees or somebody has to.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Right now, what happens is those employees get dumped into either the Medicaid system, which taxpayers pick up, or they’re going to the emergency room for uncompensated care, which everybody picks up in their premiums.

speaker: OBAMA
text: The average family is paying an additional $900 a year in higher premiums because of the uninsured.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So here’s what we do.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We exempt small businesses.

speaker: OBAMA
text: In fact, what, Joe, if you want to do the right thing with your employees and you want to provide them health insurance, we’ll give you a 50 percent credit so that you will actually be able to afford it.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If you don’t have health insurance or you want to buy into a group plan, you will be able to buy into the plan that I just described.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, what we haven’t talked about is Senator McCain’s plan.

speaker: OBAMA
text: He says he’s going to give you all a $5,000 tax credit.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That sounds pretty good.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And you can go out and buy your own insurance.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Here’s the problem — that for about 20 million people, you may find yourselves no longer having employer-based health insurance.

speaker: OBAMA
text: This is because younger people might be able to get health insurance for $5,000, young and healthy folks.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Older folks, less healthy folks, what’s going to end up happening is that you’re going to be the only ones left in your employer-based system, your employers won’t be able to afford it.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And once you’re out on your own with this $5,000 credit, Senator McCain, for the first time, is going to be taxing the health care benefits that you have from your employer.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And this is your plan, John.

speaker: OBAMA
text: For the first time in history, you will be taxing people’s health care benefits.

speaker: OBAMA
text: By the way, the average policy costs about $12,000.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So if you’ve got $5,000 and it’s going to cost you $12,000, that’s a loss for you.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Last point about Senator McCain’s plan is that insurers right now, the main restrictions on what they do is primarily state law and, under Senator McCain’s plan, those rules would be stripped away and you would start seeing a lot more insurance companies cherry-picking and excluding people from coverage.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That, I think, is a mistake and I think that this is a fundamental difference in our campaign and how we would approach health care.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: What about that?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Hey, Joe, you’re rich, congratulations, because what Joe wanted to do was buy the business that he’s been working for 10-12 hours a day, seven days a week, and you said that you wanted to spread the wealth, but — in other words, take Joe’s money and then you decide what to do with it.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, Joe, you’re rich, congratulations, and you will then fall into the category where you’ll have to pay a fine if you don’t provide health insurance that Senator Obama mandates, not the kind that you think is best for your family, your children, your employees, but the kind that he mandates for you.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: That’s big government at its best.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, 95 percent of the people in America will receive more money under my plan because they will receive not only their present benefits, which may be taxed, which will be taxed, but then you add $5,000 onto it, except for those people who have the gold-plated Cadillac insurance policies that have to do with cosmetic surgery and transplants and all of those kinds of things.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And the good thing about this is they’ll be able to go across America.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: The average cost of a health care insurance plan in America today is $5,800.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I’m going to give them $5,000 to take with them wherever they want to go, and this will give them affordability.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: This will give them availability.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: This will give them a chance to choose their own futures, not have Senator Obama and government decide that for them.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: This really gets down to the fundamental difference in our philosophies.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: If you notice that in all of this proposal, Senator — government wants — Senator Obama wants government to do the job.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Senator Obama wants government to do the job.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I want, Joe, you to do the job.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I want to leave money in your pocket.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I want you to be able to choose the health care for you and your family.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: That’s what I’m all about.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And we’ve got too much government and too much spending and the government is — the size of government has grown by 40 percent in the last eight years.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We can’t afford that in the next eight years and Senator Obama, with the Democrats in charge of Congress, things have gotten worse.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Have you noticed, they’ve been in charge the last two years.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: A short response.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Very briefly.

speaker: OBAMA
text: You all just heard my plan.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If you’ve got an employer-based health care plan, you keep it.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, under Senator McCain’s plan there is a strong risk that people would lose their employer-based health care.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s the choice you’ll have is having your employer no longer provide you health care.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And don’t take my word for it.

speaker: OBAMA
text: The U.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Chamber of Commerce, which generally doesn’t support a lot of Democrats, said that this plan could lead to the unraveling of the employer-based health care system.

speaker: OBAMA
text: All I want to do, if you’ve already got health care, is lower your costs.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That includes you, Joe.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Let’s stop there and go to another question.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: And this one goes to Senator McCain.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Senator McCain, you believe Roe v.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Wade should be overturned.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Senator Obama, you believe it shouldn’t.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Could either of you ever nominate someone to the Supreme Court who disagrees with you on this issue?

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Senator McCain?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I would never and have never in all the years I’ve been there imposed a litmus test on any nominee to the court.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: That’s not appropriate to do.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: But you don’t want Roe v.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Wade to be overturned?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I thought it was a bad decision.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I think there were a lot of decisions that were bad.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I think that decisions should rest in the hands of the states.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I’m a federalist.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I believe strongly that we should have nominees to the United States Supreme Court based on their qualifications rather than any litmus test.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, let me say that there was a time a few years ago when the United States Senate was about to blow up.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Republicans wanted to have just a majority vote to confirm a judge and the Democrats were blocking in an unprecedented fashion.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We got together seven Republicans, seven Democrats.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: You were offered a chance to join.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: You chose not to because you were afraid of the appointment of, quote, “conservative judges.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: ” I voted for Justice Breyer and Justice Ginsburg.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Not because I agreed with their ideology, but because I thought they were qualified and that elections have consequences when presidents are nominated.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: This is a very important issue we’re talking about.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Senator Obama voted against Justice Breyer and Justice Roberts on the grounds that they didn’t meet his ideological standards.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: That’s not the way we should judge these nominees.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Elections have consequences.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: They should be judged on their qualifications.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And so that’s what I will do.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I will find the best people in the world — in the United States of America who have a history of strict adherence to the Constitution.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And not legislating from the bench.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: But even if it was someone — even someone who had a history of being for abortion rights, you would consider them?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I would consider anyone in their qualifications.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I do not believe that someone who has supported Roe v.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Wade that would be part of those qualifications.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But I certainly would not impose any litmus test.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well, I think it’s true that we shouldn’t apply a strict litmus test and the most important thing in any judge is their capacity to provide fairness and justice to the American people.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And it is true that this is going to be, I think, one of the most consequential decisions of the next president.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It is very likely that one of us will be making at least one and probably more than one appointments and Roe versus Wade probably hangs in the balance.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now I would not provide a litmus test.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But I am somebody who believes that Roe versus Wade was rightly decided.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I think that abortion is a very difficult issue and it is a moral issue and one that I think good people on both sides can disagree on.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But what ultimately I believe is that women in consultation with their families, their doctors, their religious advisers, are in the best position to make this decision.

speaker: OBAMA
